protected_findings.why: Noun: the title and the Korzyść field call the same thing "powiadomienia"; here it is the vaguer "sygnały telefonu", which reads like a different object (sounds, calls). Using "powiadomienia" throughout would read more naturally and consistently, but swapping a term can change scope (alerts versus calls), so the verifier decides.

Verb: the title says "wyłącz" and Ograniczenia says "wyłączenia", while this field says "wycisz". Muting and disabling differ in intensity, so I do not harmonise them. The verifier should confirm which action the source supports and use one verb in title, W praktyce and Ograniczenia.

"opieka nad innymi" is vague and sounds translated; more natural Polish would name the people (for example "opiece nad bliskimi" or "osobami wymagającymi opieki"). The phrase names a population and touches a duty, so it is left to the verifier.

protected_findings.text: wyłączenia alarmów bezpieczeństwa lub obowiązkowego kontaktu
protected_findings.why: Two language problems. (1) Zeugma: one switches off alarms, but not a "kontakt"; the phrase would be clearer as a channel of contact, in line with "kanał kontaktu" in W praktyce. (2) "obowiązkowego" here versus "wymagany" in W praktyce names the same thing with two words, and "obowiązkowy" is a term of duty. Also the scope of "lub" is ambiguous (does "bezpieczeństwa" apply to both?). Protected wording, so reported only.
Postposed adjective is translationese; natural order is "wieloletnich skutków" (or "skutków długotrwałych"). It is a duration word, so I do not edit it.

protected_findings.text: same powiadomienia zakłócały wykonanie zadania wymagającego uwagi, nawet bez korzystania z telefonu
protected_findings.why: "same" and "nawet bez korzystania z telefonu" say the same thing twice (alone / even without use), and "bez korzystania z telefonu" is ambiguous (never touching the phone, or not picking it up). The sentence also stacks attribution (wykazali), method (w eksperymencie), a causal verb (zakłócały) and a condition, with the nominal "wykonanie zadania". Splitting into two sentences and dropping the redundancy would read better, but it touches a causal verb, an evidence verb and a limiter, so only the verifier may change it.

"zadanie uwagowe" is not an established plain Polish term and differs from "zadania wymagającego uwagi" in Korzyść i dowody, apparently for the same experiment. For consistency and first-use clarity the second wording is better, but it is a technical-term swap that I cannot check against sources, so I report it instead of editing.
